decision.comment:
Evaluation stage is complete and internally consistent. No deterministic findings are present, so no stop or mandatory revision is warranted. Test accuracy is 0.9175 (CI95 0.9110–0.9237), macro-F1 0.8849, ROC-AUC (OVR macro) 0.9755 on 7,180 held-out samples. The confusion matrix sums correctly to 7,180 and the reported accuracy (6,588/7,180 = 0.91755) matches. Selection used validation-only metrics (test_metrics_used: false), so no test leakage.

Warnings / observations (none deterministic):
1. Validation-to-test gap: best val accuracy 0.9910 vs test 0.9175 (~7.3 pp). The training curve shows no extreme overfitting (train loss still decreasing at epoch 15, early-stopping patience 3), so the gap is most plausibly attributable to distributional differences between the validation and test splits rather than overfitting. Worth documenting but not a failure.
2. Class-level performance is uneven. Cancer-associated stroma (class 7) has the lowest F1 (0.602) and recall (0.458); smooth muscle (class 5) F1 0.802; debris (class 2) F1 0.832. These are histologically similar tissue types, so cross-confusion is expected, but the stroma recall of ~46 % is a notable weakness. The remaining six classes all exceed F1 0.92.
3. Architecture coverage (carried from model_search): residual_cnn and resnet18 were never evaluated across the 8-trial budget; tiny_cnn consumed 5 of 8 trials. This is a warning-level traceability gap, not a deterministic defect, and the selected model's test performance is reasonable.
4. llm_model_digest is null in run_manifest despite llm_model='qwen3.8'. This is a reproducibility/traceability gap for LLM-in-the-loop decisions and should be populated in a future run, but it does not invalidate the current results.
5. Transformer-specific config fields (num_heads, patch_size, pooling, positional_encoding, tokenizer_layers, mlp_ratio) appear in the tiny_cnn train_config. Per pipeline rules these are inactive for CNN families and do not alter the model; noted for clarity only.
6. No OOD / corruption-severity evaluation is present in the supplied evidence. If the pipeline requires an OOD aggregate (arithmetic mean of per-severity AUROCs), that component is absent and should be added before final reporting.
7. Augmentations used (hflip, brightness, contrast) are all built-in primitives and require no extension approval. The architecture-research suggestion of ±10° rotation was not adopted; this is a traceability note, not a conflict.

Overall the evaluation is complete, mathematically consistent, and the model performs well on 7 of 9 classes. The warnings above are documentation and coverage gaps rather than correctness failures. Recommend proceeding to the next stage (e.g., OOD evaluation, final report) while addressing the noted traceability items.
issues: Validation-to-test accuracy gap of ~7.3 pp (0.9910 val vs 0.9175 test); likely distributional shift rather than overfitting, but should be documented
Cancer-associated stroma (class 7) recall is only 0.458 (F1 0.602); smooth muscle and debris also below 0.85 F1 – histologically similar classes drive most errors
Architecture coverage incomplete: residual_cnn and resnet18 never evaluated in 8-trial budget (carried warning from model_search)

No clinical claims. The supplied current UTC timestamp is authoritative. This pipeline uses the standard 28x28 RGB MedMNIST distribution; do not substitute the source-dataset or MedMNIST+ resolution. Only deterministic findings may justify action=stop; unsupported external-memory claims must be warnings requesting verification. ResNet18 has fixed topology; hidden controls base width and depth is ignored. Generic transformer fields are inactive for CNN families and do not make them transformer hybrids. Built-in augmentations (hflip, vflip, rotate90, rotate180, brightness, contrast) do not require extension approval; pending new proposals do not invalidate these primitives. A cited quote establishes traceability, not support for every scientific inference: assess that support separately. The OOD aggregate is the arithmetic mean of the selected score's AUROCs across corruption severities, not a pooled-sample AUROC.
